mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average realized Sharpe ratio during triggers is not significantly negative at 5% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 exceeding 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and causes S&P 500 to underperform over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between GDPC1 YoY decline and S&P 500 60-day returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 0.4 percentage points signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect reverses in high-inflation regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below 97 for three consecutive months indicates a contraction in industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings visibility and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between HOUST and GDPC1 where HOUST rises while GDPC1 falls signals a shift in demand composition toward housing, which historically precedes a mild equity correction as investors rotate out of cyclical stocks, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month + 1% AND GDPC1 < previous month
failure_condition: No significant predictive power (Rank IC < 0.05) or the effect reverses during high-interest-rate regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL below 2.5% indicates a successful disinflationary tightening, which boosts risk assets as inflation risk recedes, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly higher during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.3% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 0.3% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation (p > 0.10) between sustained labor growth and S&P 500 20-day returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in RSAFS below $650B for three consecutive months signals a significant drawdown in consumer savings, which reduces households' capacity for discretionary spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods (Rank IC < 0.05).
